thread.title: Earnings Roundup: AMD, Facebook, Xilinx Surge, PayPal Rises

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Earnings Roundup: AMD, Facebook, Xilinx Surge, PayPal Rises
text:
By Tiernan Ray Updated April 25, 2018 5:52 p.m. ET It’s a busy earnings afternoon, and here are some of the highlights.
Facebook ( FB ) is up $10.33, or 6.5%, at $170.02, after its Q1 revenue and profit easily topped analysts’ expectations. The company said its board of directors authorized an additional $9 billion on top of the company’s existing share-repurchase authorization of $6 billion. Jon Swartz has additional details .
Shares of chip maker Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) are up 88 cents, or 9%, at $10.59, continuing to add to gains in late trading, after the company this afternoon reported Q1 revenue and profit that comfortably beat expectations, and an outlook for revenue this quarter much higher than the Street.
Qualcomm ( QCOM ) shares initially rose 3% in late trading, but then gave up most of those gains, after the company offered a somewhat subdued outlook for this quarter’s revenue and profit.
Still, Qualcomm’s report may be something of a sigh of relief by chip investors following weeks and weeks of warnings of weaker smartphone sales, and Teradyne’s ( TER ) Apple ( AAPL ) impact in its report yesterday afternoon .
Qualcomm shares are now up 52 cents, or 1%, at $50.27.
Shares of yet another chip maker, Xilinx ( XLNX ), are up $3.71, or almost 6%, at $67.35, after the company this afternoon comfortably topped fiscal Q4 expectations, delivering $673 million in revenue and 77 cents a share in profit, versus consensus estimates for revenue of $650 million and earnings per share of 71 cents.
The outlook for this quarter, revenue of $660 million to $690 million, and EPS of 66 cents to 82 cents, is also better than the average estimate for revenue of $662 million and EPS of 71 cents.
Shares of electronic-payments pioneer PayPal Holdings ( PYPL ) are up $3.10, or 4%, at $77.10, after the company topped expectations, delivering $3.69 billion in revenue and EPS of 57 cents against consensus estimates for revenue of $3.59 billion and EPS of 54 cents.
The outlook for this quarter’s results is also higher. Emily Bary of Marketwatch has more details on the quarter .
Another winner tonight is cloud-computing software operator ServiceNow ( NOW ), its shares up $1.90, or 1.2%, at $159.90, after it reported revenue rose 37%, year-over-year, to $589 million, yielding EPS of 56 cents, versus consensus estimates for revenue of $571 million and EPS of 37 cents.
For the current quarter, the company anticipates revenue in the range from $568 million to $573 million. The Street is modeling total revenue for the quarter of $538 million, so that counts as a beat.
The one tech name inching lower this evening is networking-technology firm F5 Networks ( FFIV ), despite the company beating with its fiscal Q2 report of $533 million in revenue and EPS of $2.31, versus consensus estimates for revenue of $530 million and EPS of $2.27.
The stock is down $2.07, or 1.3%, at $155.
During the conference call following the report, the company also topped expectations, projecting revenue of $535 million to $545 million, and earnings per share of $2.36 to $2.39, versus the average estimates for revenue of $538 million and EPS of $2.37.
F5's chief financial officer , Andrew Reinland , is retiring from the company next month, and F5 announced in its earnings press release that he will be succeeded by Francis "Frank" Pelzer , who was previously COO at software giant SAP ( SAP ).
